title: Only parity makes native contradictions hard
claim: In an unsatisfiable connected closed hub-free network of three-place knots with pins, every surrounded knot (three distinct internal edges, none a bridge) is a parity knot and the rest allows exactly the complementary parity class on its edges: the rest allows at least four of the eight states and a non-parity knot at least five. Hence without parity knots every unsatisfiable native network is a cactus of odd wire cycles and has a resolution refutation whose derived clauses have at most two literals, of linear size, so such laws are decided by resolution at three literals; every unsatisfiable native network needs width at least the balanced edge boundary of its graph (flip repair, which is K2, plus hub-freeness). A parity knot is unsatisfiable on every connected cubic graph with one edge cut into two legs pinned to different values, so native contradictions are hard for resolution exactly when the law contains a parity knot (size bound conditional on Ben-Sasson and Wigderson).
failure_conditions: An unsatisfiable network with a non-parity knot that has three distinct edges and no bridge among them.
An unsatisfiable network without parity knots that is not a cactus, has a cycle that is not an odd wire cycle, or is not refuted with derived clauses of at most two literals.
A resolution refutation narrower than the balanced edge boundary on a checked parity network.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite Boolean constraint networks and resolution refutations of their clause encodings; the size corollary for parity is conditional on a cited external theorem. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library, own solver and bounded resolution) confirms the counting, Theorem 2 on 1,590 surrounded knots in 1,157 unsatisfiable random networks, Corollary 3 and Theorem 4 on 452 unsatisfiable random networks without parity knots and on necklaces of one to three rings, Theorem 5 on parity networks on the Petersen, cube and three-by-three bipartite graphs, and the cut-edge construction; four controls (connectivity, hubs, sharpness, parity not narrow). The size corollary is conditional on a cited external theorem. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with randomized and exhaustive finite checks; conditional size corollary
